questions.question: A single discount equivalent to two successive discount of 20% and 10% on the marked price of an article is?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price of an article.

**Formula used:**

Discounted price = frac{ {100 - discount}}{100} × {marked price}

**Calculation: **

Let the marked price of the article be Rs. 100.

Then, a 10% discount is (100-10)/(100) × 100 = 90 

Then, a 20% discount on Rs. 90 is Rs 72.

This means that the article marked as Rs. 100 is sold at Rs 72 which is equal to a discount of (100-72)/(100) × 100 = 28%%

**∴ A single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price of an article is 28%.**

xyz = 20

questions.question: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 94 instead of 69. Due to this error, the average marks of the class got increased by 1.25. What is the number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total change in marks = Incorrect marks − Correct marks

⇒ Total change = 94 − 69 = +25 marks

Increase in average marks per student = 1.25 marks

⇒ Number of students = Total change ÷ Average change = 25 ÷ 1.25 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Total Error = 94 − 69 = +25 marks

 Distributed as +1.25 marks per student

**Given:**

Incorrect marks entered = 94

Correct marks actual = 69

Increase in average marks of the class = 1.25 marks

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum Change = Average Change × Number of Items

**Calculations:**

Let the total number of students in the class be n.

⇒ Total difference in marks = 94 − 69

⇒ Total difference in marks = 25

This difference of 25 marks caused an increase in the overall average by 1.25 per student.

⇒ Average change × Number of students = Total difference

⇒ 1.25 × n = 25

⇒ n = 25 ÷ 1.25

⇒ n = 2500 ÷ 125

⇒ n = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Deviation Method in Averages

When a single value in a dataset is incorrectly entered, the net change in the total sum is equally distributed among all items. Average change = Total change ÷ Total items.

Replacement Formula

When one entity is replaced by another, the formula used is: New Item Value = Old Item Value + (Total Number of Items × Change in Average).

Combined Average

To calculate the net average of two combined groups, use the weighted average formula: A꜀ₒₘbᵢₙₑd = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: The value of frac{{sin 4theta }}{{( {1 - cos 4theta } )}} is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))

**Formula Used:**

sin2theta = 2 sintheta costheta

cos2theta = 2cos²theta – 1 or 1 – 2sin²theta

**Calculation:**

sin4theta=sin2(2theta)

⇒ sin4theta=2sin2theta cos2theta=2(2sintheta costheta)(1-2sin²theta)

⇒ sin4theta=4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta)

⇒ cos4theta= 2cos²2theta-1

⇒ cos4theta=2(1-2sin²theta)²-1

⇒ Putting the values, we get

⇒ (sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))=(4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta))/(1-(2(1-2sin²theta)²-1))=(4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta))/(1-(2[1+4sin⁴theta-4sin²theta]-1))

⇒ (sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))=(4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta))/(1-1-8sin⁴theta+8sin²theta)

⇒ (sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))=(4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta))/(8sin²theta(1-sin²theta))=(4sintheta costheta(1-2sin²theta))/(8sin²theta cos²theta)

⇒ (sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))=(1-2sin²theta)/(2sintheta costheta)=(cos2theta)/(sin2theta)

⇒ (sin4theta)/((1-cos4theta))=cot2theta

**∴ the required value of the given expression is cot2theta**.

questions.question: Shyamal covers 1 km in 10 min, whereas Radha covers the same distance in 8 min. By what distance does Radha beat Shyamal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Shyamal to cover 1 km = 10 min

Time taken by Radha to cover 1 km = 8 min

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

We know that 1 km = 1000 m.

If both Shyamal and Radha start together, then the distance covered by Shyamal in 8 min = (1000)/(10)×8=800 m

Now, Shyamal covers less distance than Radha.

Radha will beat Shyamal by = 1000 – 800 = 200 m.

**Hence, Radha beat Shyamal by the distance of 200 m.**

questions.question: Giri bought an old machine for ₹2,000 and spent ₹500 on its repair. He sold it for ₹4,000. His profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Price at which machine was bought = Rs 2,000

Repairment cost = Rs 500

The selling price of the machine = Rs 4,000

**Concept Used:**

Profit Percentage = (Profit)/(CP)times 100

**Calculation:**

Bought Price of machine = Rs 2,000

Repairment cost = Rs 500

Cost Price of Machine = 2000 + 500 = Rs 2,500

Profit = Selling Price – Cost Price = 4000 – 2500

Profit = Rs 1500

Now, Profit Percentage = (1500)/(2500)×100=60%.

**Hence, the profit percentage made by Giri on this machine is 60%.**

questions.question: A can do (1)/(5) of the work in 3 days and B can do (1)/(4) of the work in 7.5 days . Working together, A and B can do (4)/(5) of the same work in:

Rate of work = 1 / Time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = (1)/(5)times(1)/(3) = (1)/(15)

Time taken by B to complete the work = (1)/(4)times(1)/(7.5) = (1)/(30)

Time taken to complete the whole work together = (1)/(15)+(1)/(30)=(1)/(10) = 10 days

According to the question,

Time taken to complete (4)/(5) of the work together = (4)/(5)×10=8 days.

**Hence, the time taken by A and B, to work together to complete (4)/(5)** **of the work is 8 days.**

questions.question: The monthly income of a person was Rs. 12,000 and his monthly expenditure was Rs. 10,000. In the next year, his income increased by 12% and his expenditure by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Income : Expenditure : Savings = 12000 : 10000 : 2000 ⇒ 6 : 5 : 1.

Applying the percentage change weighted rule: (Income Ratio × % Change) = (Expenditure Ratio × % Change) + (Savings Ratio × S%)

⇒ 6 × 12 = (5 × 5) + (1 × S)

⇒ 72 = 25 + S ⇒ S = 47%

**∴ The correct answer is 47%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3c36501ea4daa12f8f67264eb492d278ce5b4a81636b45dbebebaaaa70c05bb.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹12,000

Initial Expenditure = ₹10,000

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase in value ÷ Original value) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹12,000 − ₹10,000 = ₹2,000

⇒ New Income = ₹12,000 + (12% of 12,000) = 12,000 + 1,440 = ₹13,440

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹10,000 + (5% of 10,000) = 10,000 + 500 = ₹10,500

⇒ New Savings = ₹13,440 − ₹10,500 = ₹2,940

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹2,940 − ₹2,000 = ₹940

⇒ Percentage Increase = (940 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 47%

**∴ The correct answer is 47%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Relationship

Income is the sum of Expenditure and Savings (Income = Expenditure + Savings). Any change in overall income must be balanced by an equivalent combined change in expenditure and savings.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100. It measures the relative increase or decrease of an entity over a given time period.

Weighted Ratio Trick

When a total amount is divided into distinct parts, the overall percentage change is the weighted average of the individual changes: Total Ratio × %ΔTotal = Part1 Ratio × %ΔPart1 + Part2 Ratio × %ΔPart2.
</p

questions.question: Three numbers A, B and C are in the ratio of 15 ∶ 21 ∶ 27. The ratio of the difference between B and A to the difference between C and B is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of three numbers A, B and C = 15 : 21 : 27

**Concept Used:**

The ratio of difference = Difference between A and B ÷ Difference between B and C

**Calculation:**

Let the numbers A, B and C be 15x, 21x and 27x respectively.

Difference between B and A = 21x – 15x = 6x

Difference between C and B = 27x – 21x = 6x

Ratio of these differences = (6x)/(6x)=(1)/(1)=1:1

**Hence, the ratio of the difference between B and A to the difference between C and B is 1 : 1**
